# SHA3-256 round 23: compact-controller distinguished-point search

## 1. Target and construction

The target is `sha3-256-r23-prefix-v1`: the complete padded one-block SHA3-256 hash with the first 23 Keccak-f[1600] rounds.  For a 256-bit point u split into four little-endian 64-bit words, the injective six-lane embedding writes u0,u1,u0 xor u1 xor K11 to lanes 1,6,11 and u2,u3,u2 xor u3 xor K14 to lanes 4,9,14.  All other lanes, including the `0x8000000000000006` padding lane, are fixed by the constants in the shipped generator.  Define g(u)=H_r(m(u)) xor PD.  Distinct points colliding under g give distinct 128-byte messages colliding under the complete target; xoring the same PD is bijective.

The shipped experiment source contains the frozen decisions and a bounded generator for the retained incumbent step.  It emits the native packed program and compares a Python test mirror with scalar selected-round Keccak.  The normalized plan text has SHA-256 `c3f60192dcb337e7eb845e81ed9ab7b688ad1ec7c248374780291fb9cb7998b8`.  No step, graph, allocation, polarity or encoding rule is imported at run time.

## 2. Step ISA and exact count

One bit-sliced word represents 256 walks.  The declared word-RAM machine includes `packed39` as its native static instruction format, with the opcode and fixed-width register fields stated in Appendix B.  XOR, AND, OR and NOT each cost one word operation, so the native step has 139,452 executed instructions.  Each native record is charged as the one word operation it performs; there is no separate charge for fetching or decoding.  Python and C unpackers are test mirrors outside the priced machine.  They do not execute in the search and contribute no hidden decoder to BSTEP.  The 15-operation distinguished-point prefilter and five native loop/control operations give BSTEP=139,472.  The frozen construction work is charged in Section 7.

The source bindings are:
- `experiments/compact.py`: SHA-256 `5e9c6c37ffc6e58c46386cf7ef2798249ad247fa85fc00fbf2fee2e55b24547e`.

## 3. Compact controller and table

The retained controller is rewritten in the same 32-byte fixed instruction format.  On a hit, 256 stores copy the carried planes to a 256-word scratch matrix.  A charged indexed gather loop reads one point; a charged indexed setwalk loop replaces one lane; 256 fixed loads restore the planes.  The static controller has 961 instructions and 30,752 bytes, SHA-256 `2e3ab1dfbd729907b36db892aa605186e1b6268d693f2fc5ecead1a17b44d2de`.  Appendix C is the normative emitter.  The organizer experiment invokes it, requires this byte count and hash, decodes the emitted bytes and executes setup, evalF, table probe, restart, scratch gather/setwalk, replay success, recovery and replay failure.

The table has 18,296 256-bit words and 5 slots per word, capacity U=91,480.  The effective endpoint key width is 50 bits.  Each 51-bit slot contains one written bit and 50 endpoint-key bits; the word and slot position identify the trail.  All boundary values are checked by the shipped experiment.

## 4. Search algorithm

Choose one uniform 256-bit r.  Start 256 walks at r+i.  Advance in lockstep with the bit-sliced step.  A point is distinguished with exact probability theta=703/2^121.  At each distinguished point the controller gathers the endpoint, probes every table word, inserts or replays a matching pair, then restarts the affected lane.  The replay cap is LRC=40564185382003226733193754220429312; Tb=1325914782967292795419109243400224768; the replay has 63999 bins of width 633825300114114700748351602688.  The first real predecessor collision is returned and converted to the two messages.

## 5. Probability space and H1

For comparator F, lazy sampling supplies an independent uniform image at each fresh input.  Put `n=2^256`, `q=1-theta`, `E=256*Tb`, replay-bin width `w=633825300114114700748351602688`, and `J=63999`.  The birthday lower bound after e evaluations is `G(e)=1-exp(-e(e-1)/(2n))`.  If the first image coincidence needs a tail in bin j to reach the common distinguished point, its covered contribution is

```
SUM_(j=1..J) (q^((j-1)w)-q^(jw)) * G(256*(Tb-jw)).
```

The union subtraction covers every early halt or false candidate:

- `F6`, replay-cap refusal.  Summation by parts gives `G6=q^LRC*(1+LRC*theta)`.  The bound is `2*G6*(1-exp(-E^2/(2n)-E^3/(3n^2)))*(1-E/n)^(-U)`.
- `F2`, table exhaustion.  With `mu=E*theta` and `k=U-256`, Chernoff gives `exp(-mu+k*(1+ln(mu/k)))` for at least k post-initial distinguished outputs.
- `F3`, a self-coincidence inside one trail.  The union bound is `U/(theta^2*n)`.
- Start/replay coincidence is bounded by `2^-90`.
- Endpoint-key alias is `U^2*2^-(key_bits+1)`.  This is charged at the live effective key width 50.
- `F5`, hit-cap abort.  In one lockstep step a prefilter hit requires at least one of 256 fresh images to have its top 16 bits zero, so its conditional probability is at most `256*2^-16=2^-8`.  These indicators are dominated by a binomial variable of mean `Tb/2^8`.  With `delta=2^-20` and emitted cap `floor((1+delta)*Tb/2^8)+1=5179359560383465057396081511366657`, multiplicative Chernoff gives `exp(-delta^2*Tb/(2^8*(2+delta))) < 2^-1000`.
- Decimal and formula rounding receives a further `2^-60` subtraction.

Subtracting the upper endpoints of all seven failure intervals from the lower endpoint of the covered term is one union bound.  The outward-rounded result is `0.3900000005920301699291685808790087575075447906825541973677197145095917255777770338654740143957368883`, at least 0.39.  At `Tb-2475880078570760549798248448` the outward upper endpoint is `0.3899999994818793145981678525453677411363907159834555654303139992498463309818573609469081020806494223`, below 0.39.  Thus the live Tb is the first admitted grid point.

It is embedded here and in the canonical `success-certificate` organizer experiment, which recomputes the covered sum and all failure terms at 100-digit precision, checks every outward interval and requires the union lower endpoint to reach 0.39.  Its plan binding is SHA-256 `c3f60192dcb337e7eb845e81ed9ab7b688ad1ec7c248374780291fb9cb7998b8`.

## 6. Memory

The retained non-table, non-controller regions total 424,093 bytes.  They comprise the native step/prefilter, its declared register file, 256 lane identifiers, 256 lane starts, walk state and the 16-word replay data image.  The compact controller is 30,752 bytes, scratch is 8,192 bytes and the table is 585,472 bytes.  Total peak search memory is therefore 424093+30752+8192+585472=1,048,509 bytes, below 2^20.  The bounded generator is scheduled before search; its outputs are retained and its scratch is below the same peak.

## 7. Exact operations and score

Main work is Tb*BSTEP.  The exact ledger is:

- main: 184927986610014260762694004395516148842496
- replay: 762890634479334685171174935623614070863
- rare handlers/setup: 709572259772534712863263207637869738
- preprocessing: 773294838635776
- N: 185691586816753367982578043367642239418873

The frozen plan text has SHA-256 `c3f60192dcb337e7eb845e81ed9ab7b688ad1ec7c248374780291fb9cb7998b8`. Every construction phase runs before the search. Target permutations and word operations are accounted separately:

| construction phase | operation class | target permutations | word operations | compression equivalent |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| frozen constants, polarity plan and native-step generation | word operations | 0 | 33536082444288 | 33536082444288/6233 |
| structured-constant affine basis | word operations | 0 | 16777216 | 16777216/6233 |
| incumbent parameter scan | word operations | 0 | 176740054663168 | 176740054663168/6233 |
| native assembly, data image and retained hashes | word operations | 0 | 11853056 | 11853056/6233 |
| exact compact-table and Tb replan | word operations | 0 | 562949953421312 | 562949953421312/6233 |
| controller emission, packing, hashing and package checks | word operations | 0 | 68719476736 | 68719476736/6233 |

Total preprocessing is 0 target permutations plus 773294838635776 word operations, or exactly 773294838635776/6233 target-compression units. The total N below keeps it in word operations and divides by C only once.

The exact replan charge covers at most 64 float evaluations over J bins at 2^16 word operations per bin, four 80-digit Decimal evaluations at 2^24 per bin, and 2^32 fixed work; it is rounded upward to 2^49. Controller construction is rounded upward to 2^36 and covers record emission, packing, SHA-256, decoding tests, path tests and manifest generation.

Every executed controller record costs one operation except PERM, which costs C=6233.  Division by C and upward five-decimal rounding gives time_log2 124.48625; the unrounded value is 124.48624934511718625368766909004359423912388084300442241951752139289188972732862.

## 8. Support, sensitivity and credit

The generic parallel collision method is supported by Paul C. van Oorschot and Michael J. Wiener, “Parallel Collision Search with Cryptanalytic Applications,” Journal of Cryptology 12(1):1–28 (1999), DOI 10.1007/PL00003816.  The generic entries in this track use the same aggregate random-function premise.  This construction selects no differential and claims no weakness in Keccak.  A collision-hazard deficit of epsilon can be priced by replacing the comparator pair hazard by (1-epsilon) times its value and rerunning the exact certificate; the certificate is monotone in this factor, while all circuit and memory ledgers stay unchanged.

This is a credited derivative of incumbent `61b17627-15c6-40c5-9f04-218b6e94e831` at round 23 and of our compact-controller round-24 entry `911bffce-8e7a-4502-90ab-c69a473fff48`.  The incumbent's step, native encoding, embedding and replay design are preserved; the controller/table graft and this package are new.  All needed constants, decisions, executors and checks are shipped here, so no proof step defers to another submission.

## 9. Reproduction

The organizer runs the single canonical `experiments/compact.py` only in its bounded networkless sandbox.  For the retained-step experiment ids it regenerates the native program and checks scalar Keccak.  For `exact-controller` it invokes Appendix C, emits and hashes the controller, decodes and executes those exact bytes, checks table boundaries, evaluates g on full-width points and exercises success and failure paths.  For `success-certificate` it recomputes Appendix A.  Candidate-local checks bind every number above to the frozen live-plan record.
